sections.title: Lease Economics (IFRS 16)
sections.subtitle: Store-rollout rent is financing-activity cash under IFRS 16, not an operating deduction -- these charts show what reported figures leave out

charts.annotation: Excludes lease interest (also financing-activity cash, not shown here); together the two reduce Owner FCF below reported FCF -- see the DCF's lease treatment (B).

charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

charts.annotation: SBC is zero (pre-IPO scheme closed to new grants); the FY2026 buyback is in-kind SBC via treasury shares, so the count -- not an expense line -- is the dilution check here.

charts.annotation: The gap is profit attributable to minority shareholders in franchised/JV store entities, not available to owners of the parent.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Xiaocaiyuan International Holding Ltd. (小菜園): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Xiaocaiyuan International Holding Ltd. (小菜園): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Xiaocaiyuan International Holding Ltd. (小菜園): read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Xiaocaiyuan International Holding Ltd. (小菜園): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Xiaocaiyuan International Holding Ltd. (小菜園): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

leaseBurden.title: Lease principal paid
leaseBurden.content:
Lease principal paid is the repayment-of-principal line IFRS 16 parks in financing activities for the stores' right-of-use leases -- it never reduces operating cash flow or reported FCF, even though the stores could not operate without the leased space.

For Xiaocaiyuan International Holding Ltd. (小菜園): lease principal was RMB 248.6m in FY2025 (4.7% of revenue) and lease principal + interest together were ~RMB 288m (5.4% of revenue, up from 4.4% in FY2023) as the store rollout leans more on leased sites. The DCF's Owner FCF deducts both; reported FCF does not, which is why Owner FCF (RMB 462.3m) is ~39% below reported FCF (RMB 761.1m) for FY2025.

What to watch:

  • Lease principal / EBITDA rising as the store count grows (a widening royalty on the rollout)
  • Owner FCF growth lagging reported FCF growth for the same reason

ebitdaAdjusted.title: Reported EBITDA vs Adjusted EBITDA
ebitdaAdjusted.content:
EBITDA (reported) still carries right-of-use (lease) depreciation as an expense under IFRS 16. The company's own Adjusted EBITDA adds that lease depreciation back, which is standard restaurant-sector practice but makes margins look wider than the IFRS 16 income statement supports.

For Xiaocaiyuan International Holding Ltd. (小菜園): FY2025 EBITDA was RMB 1,486.1m vs Adjusted EBITDA of RMB 1,207.7m -- the company's own measure is actually the lower figure here (it also strips other items besides adding back lease D&A), so the two series are not simply "adjusted = reported + lease D&A"; read the FY2025 annual report's reconciliation note before treating either as the cash-generative capacity of the business. Either way, neither EBITDA figure nets the lease principal and interest cash -- see the lease-burden chart above for that.

What to watch:

  • The direction and size of the gap changing (reconciliation items are disclosed each FY)
  • Valuations or comps that quote Adjusted EBITDA margins without the IFRS 16 lease-cash context

netIncomeNci.title: Net income: owners vs including non-controlling interests
netIncomeNci.content:
Net income (attributable to owners) is what accrues to Xiaocaiyuan's own shareholders. Net income including NCI adds the share of profit earned by minority shareholders in subsidiaries that are not wholly owned (e.g. joint-venture or regionally co-invested store entities).

For Xiaocaiyuan International Holding Ltd. (小菜園): the DCF and EPS both use the owners' share; the NCI gap shows how much of consolidated profit is structurally unavailable to the parent, which matters when comparing consolidated revenue growth to per-share value creation.

What to watch:

  • NCI's share of profit growing faster than owners' share (value accruing to minority partners, not shareholders)
  • Consistency of the gap -- a one-off jump suggests a new JV or acquisition structure

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Xiaocaiyuan International Holding Ltd. (小菜園): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Xiaocaiyuan International Holding Ltd. (小菜園): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Xiaocaiyuan International Holding Ltd. (小菜園): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Xiaocaiyuan International Holding Ltd. (小菜園): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Xiaocaiyuan International Holding Ltd. (小菜園): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
